newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr rallies vs yen by late Tokyo, up over one yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rallies vs yen by late Tokyo, up over one yen.

text.p: 0626 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar rallied more than one yen against the yen by late Tokyo on Thursday amid growing perceptions that 111.98 yen, hit on Tuesday, would prove its near-term floor after recent steep falls, dealers said.
Efforts by Japanese officials to halt the dollar's rapid fall and fading expectations of an imminent Japanese rate rise sparked dollar purchases by a wide range of operators.
"The dollar's recovery in the past two days convinced traders here that it has finally moved out of the downward spiral," said a senior dealer at a Japanese bank.
"Sentiment improved after the dollar did not respond negatively to the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates steady, as well as yesterday's U.S. trade data," he said.
The U.S. trade deficit shrank a large 19.3 percent in March, although its deficit with Japan rose by 8.3 percent.
Another factor that sparked the dollar's upward momentum in morning trade was news that Industrial Bank of Japan made a 10 billion yen loss from derivatives trading.

The bank said its London branch made the loss. It said the loss had been reported to British authorities and to the Japanese Finance Ministry and it had had no effect on the bank's 1996/97 earnings, to be announced on Monday.
"The news was just used for an excuse for dollar purchases," said the Japanese bank dealer."Ten billion yen is not a big amount for derivatives or forex trading," he added.

U.S. funds and Japanese trust banks were among the main buyers, with the spree absorbing sales orders by exporters. "Bids were solid, absorbing selling orders at several points such as 114.90 yen and 115.10 yen," said a bank trader.

He said given a steep fall of about 16 yen from the peak of 127.47 yen on May 1, three- to four-yen gains on the dollar were a correction within a downward trend. He said a technical correction may push the dollar as high as 119 yen, while others said it is likely to be top-heavy around 116 yen.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee meeting late on Thursday that he supports the current policy of the Bank of Japan to maintain its low interest rate policy for the time being.
This also helped reinforce expectations that no Japan rate rise was imminent, supporting the dollar.
Active mark buying against the yen, mainly from overseas operators, lent indirect support to the dollar/yen rate.

Dealers in Singapore said the mark/yen cross looked like a fairly good buy after its huge drop from the 74-75 yen levels. It was at at around at 68.30 yen at 0714 GMT after falling below 67 yen earlier this week.

A European bank dealer in Singapore said the dollar/mark would remain bid, but it would have trouble in crossing 1.7020 marks later in Europe. ---Singapore newsroom (65-8703080) ---Tatsuo Ito in Tokyo 81-3-3432-1396
